title: Enormous Is Not Dangerous
sound: -ous = /əs/ (famous, dangerous, enormous, venomous, poisonous, nervous, curious — the quiet ending that turns a thing into a description of a thing)

pages.text: Myth: enormous animals are dangerous, little animals are harmless. That famous myth is not true.
The enormous whale is harmless. The venomous jellyfish is little. Enormous is not dangerous — venomous is.
Myth: a snake is poisonous. A snake is venomous! Venomous things bite you. You bite poisonous things.
A poisonous frog is not dangerous, unless you eat it. Bright skin yells: poisonous!
Myth: sharks hunt people. Sharks are curious. A curious bite is dangerous when the teeth are enormous.
Myth: every spider is dangerous. Most are harmless. The dangerous spiders are famous, and none is enormous.
A bee is nervous, not dangerous. A nervous bee stings, then dies. Nervous is not the same as dangerous.
Myth: dangerous animals are enormous and famous. The animal that kills the most people hums in your ear.
Not enormous. Not venomous. Not poisonous. Not famous. It bites, and the blood it takes makes people sick.
So do not trust a famous myth. Enormous is not dangerous. Venomous is. Poisonous is. The most dangerous animal is as little as a nail.
